explanations.text:
[# THE FILE TREE](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:main)

on the left: the project name and its files.
  a file that holds a writing which is not compiled shows small yellow dot at the left of its row. the dot goes out when the compile passes.
a left click on a file opens that file.
if a right click on the files, a folder or empty space:
  opens a list with option: "create file" 
  if clicked:
    the new file box stands under the row you right clicked, or under the last row when you clicked empty space, and takes that row's width, over everything, in the typewriter face. 
    the grey words say: "doasfrancisco.human"

    if empty space, the box stands on the last row of the tree, and that row gives the folder: the root, or the folder it stands in.
    enter [asks the server to make that file inside that folder](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:makeNamed)
    if human:
      the box takes the bare name 
      the folder is the place it shows in 
      it makes a human file, an abstraction with no code under it. 
  pressing escape or clicking anywhere closes the box or the list.

if the server refuses, show warning on top of the reader: 
if pass, only opens the new file and marks it in the tree



[# USER OPENS FILE](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:open)

if open: 
  if for the first time, file opens at the header of the abstraction that starts open.
  the page puts the abstractions [in order](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:sorted)
  a pin points from one abstraction at another. 
  the abstraction nobody points at is the most abstract, and it goes last. 
  an abstraction that a pin points at goes above the one that holds the pin, and so on upward. among equals, the one about earlier lines goes first.

if user comes back to a file, the abstractions left open stay open as you left it, and the page stands where you had scrolled it. 
a writing box left open closes when user goes to another file.



[# THE WEB SHOWS ABSTRACTIONS](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:render)
draws an abstraction as one header line:
  a small arrow, 
  the name of its piece
  its lines. 
if file opened for the first time, [the first of the top layer of abstractions](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:topOf) start open. all others start folded the first time.
under the header the words are drawn exactly as written.

a pin whose target has an abstraction is lit;
a pin with none is muted; 
a pin the map does not hold yet, one you just typed, is [read from the target it names](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:guessAnchor). 

the bar on top says how many are open.
only as soon as anything differs from the map:
  the word "unsaved", [a compile button](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:header) shows in the page.


[# USER WRITES](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:startEdit)

a pin holds the text as it is in the map:
  the pins in their brackets, the targets visible or the code of the file, or nothing for a new abstraction. 

if click on the words:
  a box is put in their place,
  the caret is where user clicked. 

if muted pin, show name beside its words, and that name counts too

if more text is typed than the size of the box:
  the box grows until its last line shows whole, also when a line wider than the screen gives it a sideways scroll bar.
  if box grow is less than the size of the screen, grow to the bottom of screen.
  the page stays where you scrolled it. 

if escape presed, or user clicks away:
  [the box closes](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:leaveEdit) 
  the text written is kept

[if tab pressed on the box](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:indent):
  four spaces are typed where the caret is
  if lines are selected:
    each line moves four spaces right
  if shift + tab, move the line, or each selected line, four spaces left.
  box stays open

if written or the page draws again between one box and the next, human code stays in their place



[#  USER CLICKS COMPILE](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:compile)

if save clicked, 
    send the abstraction text to server 
    server writes the new abstraction text
if compile clicked, while page waits for server:
  the compile button turns faint and takes no press

if refusal, show;
  server's refusal, 
  the file it came from in the warning colour, 
  and abstraction stays on web. 

if pass:
  delete the draft, redraw the page with [the map again](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:reloadMap)



# NEW ABSTRACTION

if file with no map:
    shows on top "new abstraction", if code file, show the code of the file under it. 
    the bar says there is no abstraction yet
    if new abstraction clicked, show in its place "decompile <filename>"

if right click on abstraction header, [show](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:menuAt) two options:
    ["create abstraction"](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:create)
    ["delete abstraction"](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:deleteOpen)

    if delete, show option in replace of head abstraction
    if any clicked: sends it to server
    if cancel, or escape, [close](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:deleteClose). 

if right click on [text hightlighted](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:selectedRaw)
    show option to expand abstraction
    if clicked:
        [show on top of the list](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:expandOpen) a place a user can write abstraction or none
        if click on expand: [send to server](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:expandSend)
    if cancel, close

options float a little menu from pointer, each row lights under the pointer.
each option wear a lively color and underlines itself under the points
 
if abstraction compiling, 
    show "compiling" message next to header abstraction
    if more than one, show count



[#  USER JUMPS TO ANOTHER FILE](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:crossJump)

if pin clicked, 
  open that file,,pin scrolls to the abstraction it points at, unfolds it, and lights it for a moment; it opens no box.
  if pin points to file the project does not hold, show muted and the piece name.
  if the file has no map:
    open the file, go to the lines of that file and lights them for a moment.

  if pin points to one abstraction of that file and words inside it: 
    a click opens the file, 
    goes to that abstraction,
    lights those words for a moment. 

    such a pin to words the abstraction does not hold is muted and shows the file and the number of the abstraction (explain this line?)
  
  [save](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:keepPlace):
    place of the abstraction or file left.
    the file, the abstractions open it it, scroll position.

if back button of the browser, alt and left, the back button of the mouse, or a swipe back on a phone, pressed: 
    [return to the previous place kept](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:goPlace).
if forward button, or alt and right pressed, return to the next place kept.
in both cases, if writing box left open, it closes when you go back



[# WEB DESIGN](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:style)

a dark and a light version, chosen by your system. 
font is SF Pro, the San Francisco font of Apple. If not apple device, use typewriter font.
[sintax highlight](compiler/cli/human/reader/web.html:colours) for code files using shiki 4.5.0
side and vertical scroll ui, small pill, no bar, and fades.


two panes on a quiet ground: 
    the tree on the left, 
    the reader on the right, as wide as the window lets it.


the tree looks like the list of apple notes:
    dark: #0b0b0b
    light: the soft grey ground of apple notes, #f2f2f7.
    the project name shows in upper case.
    the tree is below, same indent as the project name
    file names in off-white, folder names and icons in grey #8e8e93.
    the open file wears a lighter grey row, no lively colour.

    if on a narrow screen:
        the tree sits in a card: dark grey #1c1c1e, or white in light, with large round corners and no edge.
        the tree hides and slides in over the reader. if tree opens, the reader section appears dark fading

the reader:
  dark: pure black ground, off-white words, like apple notes.
  light: pure white ground, near-black words.
  caret is dark yellow and slightly thick
  caret stays right after the last letter on a line of any length
  the buttons are dark grey glass with a thin lighter edge, white icons.
  
  the reader fills the screen, no frame.
  the reader separates from the file tree with a faint soft grey line

  the file name and count show in the same filled screen. horizontally centered. top division has no line divider.
  
  top right, one pill holding the lucide icon button floats over words, like the pills of apple notes: 
    a filled green play for compile, the icon shows a bit smaller than default for better design
  
  a non-pill, #e0ae01 filled circle with a #fff65c save icon inside to save:
    almost as big as the pill buttons, a bit smaller so it looks good
    apppears in an animation, on the right of compile
    enough space to not press compiler by mistake. 
    if clicked, file saves. 
  the buttons use the black ground, the grey glass and the white icons, with no lively colour. same height as the file name and count

  the text fades on the top and bottom.
  if highlighting the text, the highlight color is yellow
  a tip note is dark grey glass with round corners, white words and a dark yellow "got it" at its right
  the arrow of a new change is green, bold, in a handwritten font, and floats slowly up and down; it takes no click
  font size 14px
  a line wider than the screen scrolls sideways. 
        
  if on a narrow screen:
    the colour of the reader fills the whole screen
    the words font:
      size is 14px
      they keep that size when you read and when you write. specially in safari mobile.
  
    sideway scroll at furthest at the bottom
    the file name and the count do not show
    
    the top bar has no line of its own. 
    top left, a round button with the burger in a center floats over the words. it opens the tree.


    if click on a header, folds or unfolds that abstraction.

    a redraw of the same file keeps the page where you had scrolled it, so the words stay under your eyes. 
    
    if click away, current open box closes
    
    the writing box and grows with text typed and sits in the text place
    an empty text boxt has place and lights up under the pointer
